title: 02. Data Structures: QUEUE, HEAPQ & PRIORITY STRUCTURES
summary: QUEUE, HEAPQ & PRIORITY STRUCTURES: explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/queues_heaps.py
import heapq
from queue import Queue, LifoQueue, PriorityQueue
from collections import deque

# ============================================================
# HEAPQ — Min-Heap (Priority Queue via list)
# ============================================================
# Always maintains smallest element at index 0

nums = [5, 3, 8, 1, 2, 7]
heapq.heapify(nums)            # Convert list to heap in-place O(n)
print(nums)                     # [1, 2, 7, 5, 3, 8]

heapq.heappush(nums, 0)       # Add element O(log n)
smallest = heapq.heappop(nums) # Remove smallest O(log n)
print(smallest)                 # 0

# Push and pop in one operation
replaced = heapq.heapreplace(nums, 10)  # Pop smallest, push 10
# heappushpop — push first, then pop (slightly different)

# --- Top N elements ---
data = [10, 4, 5, 1, 8, 3, 7, 9, 2, 6]
print(heapq.nlargest(3, data))   # [10, 9, 8]
print(heapq.nsmallest(3, data))  # [1, 2, 3]

# With key function
tasks = [("low", "task1"), ("high", "task2"), ("medium", "task3")]
print(heapq.nlargest(2, tasks, key=lambda x: x[0]))

# --- Max Heap (negate values) ---
max_heap = []
for val in [5, 3, 8, 1]:
    heapq.heappush(max_heap, -val)  # Negate!

largest = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)  # Negate back!
print(largest)  # 8

# --- Merge sorted iterables ---
merged = list(heapq.merge([1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6], [0, 7, 8]))
# [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]

# --- Priority Queue with custom objects ---
import dataclasses

@dataclasses.dataclass(order=True)
class Task:
    priority: int
    name: str = dataclasses.field(compare=False)

task_heap = []
heapq.heappush(task_heap, Task(2, "Medium task"))
heapq.heappush(task_heap, Task(1, "High priority"))
heapq.heappush(task_heap, Task(3, "Low priority"))

print(heapq.heappop(task_heap))  # Task(priority=1, name='High priority')

# ============================================================
# QUEUE MODULE — Thread-Safe Queues
# ============================================================

# --- FIFO Queue ---
q = Queue(maxsize=10)
q.put("first")
q.put("second")
print(q.get())        # "first" (FIFO)
print(q.qsize())      # 1
print(q.empty())      # False

# --- LIFO Queue (Stack) ---
stack = LifoQueue()
stack.put("first")
stack.put("second")
print(stack.get())    # "second" (LIFO)

# --- Priority Queue (thread-safe) ---
pq = PriorityQueue()
pq.put((2, "medium"))
pq.put((1, "high"))
pq.put((3, "low"))
print(pq.get())       # (1, 'high')

# --- Blocking behavior (great for producer-consumer) ---
import threading

def producer(q: Queue):
    for i in range(5):
        q.put(f"Item {i}")
    q.put(None)  # Sentinel to signal done

def consumer(q: Queue):
    while True:
        item = q.get()  # Blocks until item available
        if item is None:
            break
        print(f"Consumed: {item}")
        q.task_done()

q = Queue()
t1 = threading.Thread(target=producer, args=(q,))
t2 = threading.Thread(target=consumer, args=(q,))
t1.start(); t2.start()
t1.join(); t2.join()
```
